transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, hi. Um, well, what brings me in is... I just, I hardly eat right anymore. Like, I don't even know when it started getting this bad exactly, but I just can't seem to put real food down. Some days, and I mean a whole lot of days lately, it is literally just coffee. I'll wake up and pour a cup just to have something warm in my stomach, and maybe... maybe later on I'll grab a piece of bread. Not even a sandwich, you know, just a plain slice of white bread straight out of the bag because I just can't be bothered to put anything on it or cook a real meal. 

And it's really starting to show, too. My pants are just hanging loose on me now. I had to dig out this old belt I haven't worn in years just to keep my jeans from falling down to my ankles when I walk around the house, and even then they look all baggy and ridiculous on me. I just look down and see how much weight I've dropped, and I know it ain't right to just live on coffee and a piece of crust. But I just look at food and I don't want it. It's just... it's really messed up my body, being this skinny all of a sudden, and I just don't know how to get my stomach working right again.
Have you been trying to lose weight?

No, no, Lord no. I ain't trying to go on no diet or nothing like that. I mean, why would I be doing that on purpose? I ain't got no job to look fancy for, I ain't trying to be on TV or impress nobody. It's just... I don't know, it's like my stomach just flat out shut off. 

You know how when you're sick with a bug or something, and the very thought of, like, a heavy meal just makes your guts turn over? It's like that, but every single day. I'll go into the kitchen and open the fridge, right? And I'll just stand there with the door open, feeling that cold air, and I'll look at the cheese, or the lunch meat I bought Lord knows how long ago—it's probably gone bad by now anyway—and I just feel... tired. Just looking at it makes me tired. The chewing, the swallowing, figuring out what to put on a plate... it all just feels like way too much work for a guy who's just sitting at home anyway. 

So no, I ain't trying to lose a single pound. If anything, I wish I could just sit down and eat a normal plate of food like I used to, maybe a big bowl of chili or something, but my body just says nope. It's real frustrating, you know? Because people see you getting all bony and they probably think you're doing it on purpose, but I'm just sitting there staring at a piece of bread wishing I actually wanted to eat the damn thing.
Are you ever afraid of gaining weight?

Afraid of it? Man, no. Heck no. If anything, I'd pay good money to gain some weight right about now. Like I was just saying with that old belt and my jeans... I want to actually fill out my clothes again, you know? I look in the mirror sometimes, like right after I get out of the shower, and I just see these ribs poking out all sharp, and my collarbones looking like they're trying to punch right through my skin, and it just looks plain awful. Why in the world would I be scared of putting some meat back on my bones? I ain't trying to be no underwear model or nothing. I'm just a regular guy who wants to look regular again. 

If I woke up tomorrow and stepped on the scale and saw I put on ten pounds, or even if I just had a little bit of a gut starting to show, I'd probably throw a damn party. I really would. I'd go down to the store and buy something to celebrate, even if I couldn't stomach eating it. It's just... the whole idea of being scared of getting fat when you're practically blowing away in the wind, it just don't make a lick of sense to me. 

I used to be a pretty sturdy guy, you know? Not heavy, but solid. Like I could hold my own. Now I'm just... I don't know, frail. I hate that word, especially for a guy my age, but that's what it is. Frail. I bump into a doorframe and it feels like I'm gonna bruise down to the bone. So no, doc, I ain't scared of gaining weight one bit. I'm practically praying for it, honestly, I just can't get the food down to make it happen.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah... yeah, I really have. And it's a crying shame, honestly, because I didn't used to be this way. I used to have things that kept me busy, you know? Like, I used to love going for walks down by the lake. Just taking my time, walking along the water, watching the ducks or the folks fishing, just breathing in the fresh air. It used to make me feel real peaceful, just being out there and moving my legs. And when I was at home, I had my little model kits. I'd set up at the card table in the corner of the living room with the little bottles of glue and the tiny little decals, and I could sit there for hours putting together a classic Chevy or a fighter plane. I had real patience for it. I'd get the tweezers out and make sure every little piece was sitting just right. It was my thing, you know? It gave me something to do with my hands since I ain't working.

But now... man, I don't know. Now I don't even step foot near that lake. The thought of putting on my shoes and walking all the way down there just seems so pointless, like, what am I even walking around for? And my models... they just sit there. I've got one half-finished on the table right now, a '68 Mustang, and the dust is just piling up on the little plastic windshield. I look at it, and I look at the ones I finished sitting up on the shelf, and I swear to you, doc, it's like they belong to somebody else. 

Like some other guy sat there and built 'em, and I'm just sitting in his house looking at his stuff. I just stare at them and I don't feel a single itch to pick up the glue or finish painting the engine block. It's just pieces of plastic to me now. I don't get no joy out of it, no spark, nothing. I just sit in my chair and look at the box, and I can't for the life of me remember why I ever cared about putting it together in the first place. It's like the part of my brain that actually liked doing things just dried up and blew away, leaving me with nothing to do but just sit there.
Do you often feel sad or down?

Yeah... yeah, I do. It's like... well, it's like this heavy, empty feeling right here in my chest, you know? Just sitting there like a rock. Most days, I wake up, and before I even open my eyes, before I even swing my legs over the side of the bed to put my feet on the floor, I can feel it waiting for me. It's just this awful, sinking feeling that nothing good is going to happen today, that there ain't nothing waiting for me out there but more of the same. 

I'll just lay there looking at the ceiling, watching the light change as the morning goes on, and I just think, what's the point of even getting up? There's no job to go to, no one waiting on me, and even if there was, I just... I just want to keep my head down, you know? Just pull the covers right back up over my ears and hide away from the whole world. It's like I'm wearing a lead apron, the kind they put on you at the dentist when they take x-rays, but it's on the inside. 

And it ain't just a fleeting thing, doc. It's most days. It's like a dark cloud that just parked itself right over my house and refuses to blow away. Sometimes I'll be sitting in my chair, just staring at the wall or the TV when it ain't even turned on, and I'll realize I've been sitting there for hours just feeling... sad. Not the kind of sad where you cry because you watched a sad movie or someone passed away, but just this deep, hollow, down-in-the-dumps kind of sad that you can't shake loose no matter how hard you try. It just drains the life right out of you, makes you feel like you're just existing instead of living. So yeah, I feel down pretty much all the time lately. It's exhausting, it really is.
Do you think you would enjoy your walks or model kits again if you were feeling physically better and had more energy?

I don't... I don't think so, doc. I really don't. Because, see, it ain't just about being tired or feeling weak. Like I was saying just a minute ago about the lake and those little model kits... it's a whole lot deeper than just not having the juice in my batteries, you know? 

Even if I woke up tomorrow and felt like a million bucks, physically speaking, I don't think it would change a single thing. Because the problem ain't my legs being too worn out to walk down to the water, and it ain't my hands being too heavy to hold the little tweezers for the decals on the cars. It's... it's my head. Or my heart, maybe. I don't rightly know. 

Like I said, I look at that '68 Mustang sitting there on the card table in the living room, and it really does feel like it belongs to somebody else entirely. If I had all the energy in the world, I'd still just be staring at a stranger's pieces of plastic. The part of me that actually got a kick out of it, the part that cared if the silver paint on the engine block was perfectly even or if the ducks at the lake were getting enough bread... that part is just gone. 

It's like somebody came in while I was sleeping and snipped the wire that connects me to the things I used to like. I can see the models, I can remember that I used to like them, but I can't *feel* it. So, sure, if I had more energy, maybe I'd be standing up instead of sitting in my chair when I look at 'em, or maybe I'd pace around the room, but I'd still be looking at 'em like they ain't mine. I just don't have it in me to care about 'em anymore, energy or no energy. It's just a totally dead feeling.
Do you think you would enjoy things like your walks or model kits if you actually did them, or is it more that you just can't seem to get started?

Well... see, that's the thing, doc. Like I was just saying a minute ago about how they feel like they belong to some other guy... it ain't just about getting the engine running, so to speak. It's not just that I can't get out of the chair. Because, truth be told, I have tried. I really have. 

I've forced myself to sit down at that card table in the living room, right in front of that '68 Mustang. I've picked up the little plastic pieces, held the little tube of glue in my hand, and tried to make myself just... I don't know, just glue the bumper on. Just one piece, I told myself. But even sitting right there, actually trying to do it, holding the things in my own two hands... nothing. There's just no spark. I'm just a guy holding a piece of plastic. I don't care if it gets glued on straight or crooked or if it gets glued on at all. It's exactly like I said, I look at my own hands doing it and it feels like somebody else's hobby. 

And the lake, too... say somebody drove me down there and pushed me out the car door right onto the walking path. I'd just be standing there looking at the water, and I wouldn't care about the ducks or the folks fishing or the fresh air. I wouldn't enjoy it one bit. It's not that I just can't get started, it's that the part of me that actually liked doing those things... it's just completely gone. Like I told you, I used to really like walking by the lake and working on my little model kits, I really did, but now... now they just sit there, and even if I force myself to touch 'em, I just look at them like they belong to somebody else entirely. Doing it doesn't bring the feeling back. The feeling is just dead.
Do you often feel guilty about anything?

Yeah... yeah, I do. All the time, doc. It just eats at me, you know? It's like this heavy weight sitting right on my chest, right next to that empty feeling I was telling you about before. It's just... I keep thinking about how I'm just no good. I mean, look at me. I'm 35 years old, and I ain't even working. 

Ever since I lost that job... well, I just can't stop thinking about it. It plays over and over in my head like a broken record. Every little mistake I made, every time I messed up, every time I should have done something different... I just replay it, sitting there in my chair, staring at the wall. I just keep thinking about how I ruined everything. I had a job, I was doing okay, and then I just blew it. And now? Now I'm just a burden. 

My relatives, they have to help me out, and I just feel so ashamed. They work hard for their money, and here I am, taking it because I can't even get myself together enough to earn my own keep. I should be the one helping them, you know? I should be standing on my own two feet. But instead, I'm just sitting in that chair, looking at those models I don't care about, and thinking about how useless I am. It's just this constant, nagging guilt that I'm dragging everybody else down with me. I feel like I'm just taking up space, wasting air that somebody else could be using. It's just... it's a terrible feeling, doc, knowing you're the reason things are so messed up and knowing you can't even fix it because you don't even have the energy to care about a plastic Mustang anymore. It just makes me feel completely worthless, from the time I wake up till the time I finally manage to get to sleep.
Have you ever thought about harming yourself?

No... no, I ain't ever thought about doing nothing like that. I know I was just saying how useless I feel, and how I'm just taking up space and dragging my folks down... and it's true, I feel that way all the time, just sitting there in that chair while the world goes on without me. It's a heavy, heavy thing to carry around, feeling like a burden, feeling like you messed up your whole life at 35 and can't even glue a piece of plastic onto a model car anymore. 

But as bad as it gets, and as much as I replay all those mistakes in my head until I feel like I'm going crazy with the guilt of it all... I ain't ever thought about hurting myself. I don't want to die, doc. I just... I just don't know how to live right now. It's like I'm stuck in this gray area where I'm not really alive, because I don't care about the lake or the ducks or the Mustangs, but I ain't looking to end it all, neither. I just sit there and let the guilt eat at me, but I've never once picked up a knife or looked at a bottle of pills and thought about checking out early. I just... I just sit there, you know? Just taking up space. But no, no thoughts about harming myself. None at all.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, let's see... it's been a while now. This whole thing, this heavy, gray cloud just sitting right on top of me... it's been hanging over me for about five months now. 

I remember because it was right around the time the weather started turning, you know? The leaves were just starting to change, and I was sitting in my chair, looking out the window, and I just realized... I realized I hadn't touched a model kit in weeks. I hadn't been down to the lake. And that feeling, that emptiness I was telling you about, it just sort of settled in right then. Five months of just... sitting there. Five months of staring at the wall, thinking about the job I lost, thinking about how I'm just a burden on my folks. 

It feels like a lot longer, to be honest with you, doc. When you're just sitting there, day in and day out, not caring about anything, not having the energy to even glue a piece of plastic... the days just drag on forever. You wake up, and you're already tired, and you know you got nothing to look forward to, so you just sit there. And then the sun goes down, and you try to sleep, but your brain is just spinning with all the guilt and all the mistakes. So yeah, it's been five months of this. Five months of just being completely stuck in this rut, feeling like I'm not really alive, but not wanting to die neither. Just... five months of nothing.
Do you think your lack of interest in things like walks and model kits is more because of the sad thoughts you've been having or because you're just too tired to do them?

Well, doc... it's kind of hard to pull those two things apart, you know? The sad thoughts, the guilt, the emptiness... they're always there, playing on a loop. But the tired part... man, the tired part is just something else entirely. It's not just feeling sleepy, like you didn't get enough shut-eye the night before. It's this deep, heavy kind of tired that just sinks right into your bones. 

I mean, I'll be sitting there in my chair, looking over at my work table where my model kits are, and I might think, for just a split second, 'Maybe I'll go glue a piece on that Mustang today.' But then I try to move, and it's like... it's like my arms and legs are full of wet sand. Just heavy, dragging, dead weight. It takes everything I have just to stand up. 

It's not even just the models or the walks down by the lake. It's everything. Even taking out the trash... I'll look at the bag sitting by the door, and I know it needs to go out, but just the thought of picking it up, walking out the door, lifting the lid on the can... it feels like I'm trying to climb a mountain. It's just too much. Even coming here to the clinic today, getting dressed, getting out the door, sitting in the waiting room... it completely wiped me out. I feel like I ran a marathon, and all I did was put on my shoes and walk into your office. 

So, yeah, the sad thoughts are there, and they make it hard to care about things, but the tiredness... it's physical, doc. It's like gravity is turned up double just for me. I just sit there because moving is too hard. It's like the energy just drained right out of my toes five months ago and never came back. So even if I wanted to build a model, even if I could get past the guilt and the emptiness for five minutes... I don't think I could lift my arms long enough to do it. The wet sand just holds me down in that chair, day after day.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your sleep patterns over the past five months?

Sleep... man, sleep is just a whole other mess. You'd think, since I'm so tired, like I was just saying about the wet sand and all, that I'd just close my eyes and be out like a light. But it ain't like that. Not at all. 

Lately, I go lay down in my bed, right? And the house gets all quiet... my folks are asleep, ain't no cars going by outside... and I just lie there. For hours, doc. Just staring at the wall, watching the shadows from the streetlamp outside my window just stretch across the paint. My body feels like dead weight, but I just can't drift off. I'll just lie there staring, replaying every dumb thing I ever did in my life. 

And then, if I finally do manage to fall asleep, it's like my brain decides that's enough, and my eyes just pop open way before the sun even comes up. It'll be pitch black out, maybe three or four in the morning, the birds ain't even making noise yet, and I'm just awake. I'll try to force my eyes shut, try to roll over and get comfortable, but I just cannot get back to sleep. I just lay there waiting for the morning, which I don't even want to come anyway since I got nothing to do but sit in my chair. 

And the real kicker is, doc... even when I do sleep, even when I get a few hours in between all that staring at the wall and waking up in the dark, I don't feel rested at all. Not one bit. I wake up and I feel completely worn out, like I spent the whole night digging ditches instead of laying on a mattress. It's just exhausting. The night is just as heavy and exhausting as the day, maybe even worse because there ain't nothing to distract you from it. So yeah, my sleep has been completely messed up for a long time now.
Do you think your lack of interest in things like walks and model kits would change if your sadness and guilt went away?

Well, doc... that's a tough one to figure. I mean, if the sadness and all that guilt just packed up and left? I don't know. It's hard to even picture what that would look like, because right now, that guilt is just... it's everywhere. It's like breathing it in, you know? 

Because, see, I sit in that chair, and my mind just goes right to the job. That job I lost. And I think, man, I am just no good. I'm completely useless. I lost that job, and now I'm just sitting here, taking up space, and my folks... my poor folks, they have to help me out. They have to put a roof over my head and food on my plate, and I'm a grown man. I should be taking care of them, not the other way around. It just eats at me, doc. It really does. 

And it's not just the job, either. It's like my brain just wants to punish me. I sit there, and I just replay every single mistake I ever made in my entire life. Every wrong turn, every dumb thing I said, every time I messed up... it just plays on a loop, over and over and over. Like a movie I can't turn off. And I just sit there thinking about how I ruined everything. I ruined my life, I ruined my chances, I'm ruining my parents' retirement by being this... this burden. 

So, if all that went away? If I didn't feel like I was just this worthless piece of garbage dragging everybody down? Maybe. Maybe I'd want to go down to the lake. Maybe I'd look at that Mustang kit and actually want to put the decals on. But honestly, doc, right now, I can't even imagine not feeling this way. I can't imagine a morning where I don't wake up and immediately start beating myself up for being such a failure. It's just so loud in my head, all the time, telling me how bad I messed up. So... I guess the answer is maybe, but it feels like a really, really big maybe. Because right now, the guilt is just... it's all there is.
How long have you felt like you didn't care about the things you used to enjoy, like your walks and model kits?

Five months, doc. It’s been right about five months now that this whole... this depressed spell has just been hanging over me. I mean, it honestly feels like it’s been a whole lot longer than that, just because every single day drags on so much when you're just sitting in a chair, but yeah, five months. 

I remember it pretty clear, too, because I had just bought the paint for that Mustang kit. The good enamel paint, you know? Candy apple red and a little bottle of silver for the chrome bumpers. I had the box sitting out on the little folding card table I use in my bedroom, all the little plastic pieces laid out, the glue right there... and I just couldn't do it. I just looked at it one morning, about five months ago, and I felt absolutely nothing. No excitement, no drive to put it together, just... nothing. 

And the walks... man, I used to really like walking down by the lake. I’d go down there, skip a few rocks, just watch the water ripple. It was quiet, you know? Peaceful. But right around that same time, five months back, the idea of even putting on my boots to go down there just... it just vanished. It’s like someone came into my head and just unplugged the part of me that actually liked doing things. You'd think after a week or two, a guy would snap out of it, right? You'd think the dust on the model box would bother me enough to at least put it away. But no. Day after day, week after week... it just stretches on. So for five whole months, that Mustang has just been sitting there, and I haven't been down to the water once. Just five months of this heavy cloud hanging over me.
Do you feel any pleasure when you do manage to engage in activities, even if it's just for a brief moment?

Pleasure? No... no, doc, not even for a second. Not even a tiny little spark. 

I mean, I try, you know? Sometimes I'll get up from the chair and I'll walk over to that little folding table I was telling you about, just to see. Just to test it out, I guess. I'll pick up one of the little plastic pieces, maybe the little engine block or one of the tires for that Mustang, and I'll just hold it in my hand. I'll stand there waiting for something to happen, waiting to feel even just a drop of excitement about putting it together, but... nothing. Absolutely nothing happens. 

I used to really like working on my little model kits, doc. I used to spend hours just getting the decals perfectly straight, making sure there wasn't any glue showing on the seams. And I used to like walking by the lake, too, just being out there in the air. But now... now they just sit there. The model kit just sits on the table collecting dust, and the lake is just... out there, and I don't care about either of them. 

And the really crazy part, the thing that really messes with my head when I stand there holding that little plastic car part, is that I look at it... and I look at them like they belong to somebody else. Like some other guy bought that paint. Like some stranger set up that table in my room and I'm just looking at his stuff. It doesn't feel like mine anymore. It's like the guy who enjoyed those things just packed up and left, and I'm just the empty shell he left behind in the room. So I just put the piece back down on the cardboard box, exactly where I found it, and I go right back to my chair. Because what's the point? There's just no joy in it. Not even for a split second. It's all just dead to me now.
Do you feel like you're a burden to others most of the time?

Like I was saying a few minutes ago, doc... yeah. That's exactly it. It's all the time. I just keep thinking I am no good, you know? I mean, I lost that job, and now... now my relatives, my folks, they have to help me with every little thing. I'm thirty-five years old. I didn't even make it past the eighth grade, I dropped out way back in the day, but I always managed to work. I always pulled my own weight, at least. And now I can't even do that. Now I'm just this heavy weight around their necks. 

And it’s not just a passing thought, either. It’s all day long. I sit in that chair and my brain just starts going, and I replay every single mistake I’ve ever made in my entire life. Like I was telling you before about that movie loop in my head? It just keeps rolling and rolling. Every time I messed up, every time I let somebody down, every dumb choice... it just plays and plays until I feel like I ruined everything. I ruined my own life, and now I'm ruining theirs because they have to spend their time and their money taking care of a grown man who can't even get it together to go outside or put a plastic car together. 

It’s just... it’s unbearable, doc. You try to tell yourself that maybe it’s not that bad, maybe people hit rough patches, but then you look at the reality of it, and you realize you're just taking up space. You're just a drain on the people who actually care about you. So yeah, "burden" is exactly the word for it. I just feel like I'm dragging everybody down with me, and I can't seem to stop doing it.
Do you feel like your current state is the worst it's been, or have you had periods where you felt even lower?

Well, doc, that's... that's a tough one to answer, because it's not like it's a straight line, you know? But honestly, I think this right now... this is the lowest. I really do. Because most days, I wake up, and before I even open my eyes, before I even swing my legs out of bed, I just feel this... this heavy, empty feeling right here in the middle of my chest. It's like a physical weight pressing down on me, just sitting right on my ribs. 

And it's there every single morning. I wake up with it, and my first thought is always just... there's nothing good waiting for me today. There's no point in getting up. It's like the whole day is already ruined before the sun even comes up properly. I just want to keep my head down, you know? Pull the covers back up, bury my face in the pillow, and just disappear. 

I remember back when I was working, even if I was tired, even if my back was hurting from being on my feet all day, I'd wake up and at least think, "Okay, gotta go make a dollar, gotta go see the guys." There was something. But now? Now it's just this massive, gaping hole in my chest. It's so empty, but somehow it weighs a ton. And it just makes me want to shrink down until I'm nothing. So yeah, I don't think I've ever felt this low before. This five-month stretch... waking up with that heavy chest every single day, just knowing there's absolutely nothing out there for me... it's definitely the worst it's ever been. I can't imagine it getting any lower than this, honestly. I just can't.
Have you ever had thoughts of suicide or attempted to harm yourself during these past five months?

No... no, doc, I haven't. I mean, I know I just sat here and told you how bad it is, how I wake up with that heavy chest and how I just want to disappear into the mattress, and I know it probably sounds like I'd want to just end it all. I get that. Anybody listening to me talk about being a burden and staring at the wall all day would probably think, "This guy is gonna do something drastic." But... I haven't. I really haven't. 

I don't know if it's because I'm scared, or if it's because of my folks... you know, I think about them a lot. I think about how much they're already doing for me, letting me stay there, feeding me, basically keeping me alive since I lost the job. And I think, if I did something like that, if I actually tried to hurt myself or... or kill myself... well, that would just be the ultimate burden, wouldn't it? I mean, then they'd have to deal with the police, and the ambulance, and the funeral, and... and the guilt. I couldn't do that to them. I feel bad enough just taking up space in the spare room. 

So no, I don't sit there planning anything. I don't look at the pills in the bathroom cabinet or think about doing anything violent. It's more like... I just wish I wasn't here. There's a difference, you know? Like, I wish I could just push a button and erase myself so nobody had to remember me, but actually taking a step to do it myself? No. I haven't tried to hurt myself, not once in these five months. I just sit in the chair. I just sit there and let the days pass, even though it feels like torture. But I haven't crossed that line, doc. I really haven't.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from any activities, or is it just the ones you used to enjoy that don't bring you joy anymore?

Well, doc, it's... it's really everything. It's not just that I don't care about the stuff I used to like, it's that nothing feels good anymore. Nothing at all. I mean, you asked about the things I used to enjoy, right? I used to like walking by the lake. There's this little spot, maybe a mile from my folks' place, where the trees kind of bend over the water, and I'd go down there in the evenings. It was quiet, you know? Just me and the ducks, watching the sun go down. It used to make me feel kind of settled. And I had these little model kits I'd work on. Cars, mostly. Classic muscle cars. I had a whole setup on this folding table in the corner of my room, with the tiny paintbrushes and the glue that smells like chemicals, and I'd sit there for hours just getting the decals perfectly straight. 

But now... man, now they just sit there. The models, the paints, everything. I look at them, and it's like... it's like they belong to somebody else. Some other guy who used to live in my room and actually cared about putting a tiny plastic steering wheel into a tiny plastic dashboard. I look at them and I don't feel a single thing. No urge to pick them up, no interest in finishing the ones I started. They're just gathering dust. 

And it's not just the models or the lake. It's food, too. My mom made my favorite meatloaf last week—she spent all afternoon on it, trying to cheer me up, bless her heart—and I put it in my mouth and it just tasted like ash. Like cardboard. I chewed it and swallowed it because I didn't want to hurt her feelings, but there was no joy in it. No flavor, really. And watching TV? I used to love those old Westerns, but now the TV is just noise. Just moving colors on a screen. I sit in that chair and stare at it, but I'm not really watching. I don't care what happens to the cowboy or the sheriff. I just don't care. 

So, yeah, it's everything. It's like somebody came in and just unplugged me from... from life, I guess. Nothing brings me any kind of pleasure, not the old stuff, not new stuff, nothing. It's all just flat. Just completely, utterly flat and gray, all day, every day.

The night is just as heavy and exhausting as the day, maybe even worse because there ain't nothing to distract you from it. So yeah, my sleep has been completely messed up for a long time now.

patient.answer:
Well, doc... that's a tough one to figure. I mean, if the sadness and all that guilt just packed up and left? I don't know. It's hard to even picture what that would look like, because right now, that guilt is just... it's everywhere. It's like breathing it in, you know?

I lost that job, and now I'm just sitting here, taking up space, and my folks... my poor folks, they have to help me out. They have to put a roof over my head and food on my plate, and I'm a grown man. I should be taking care of them, not the other way around. It just eats at me, doc. It really does.

Every wrong turn, every dumb thing I said, every time I messed up... it just plays on a loop, over and over and over. Like a movie I can't turn off. And I just sit there thinking about how I ruined everything. I ruined my life, I ruined my chances, I'm ruining my parents' retirement by being this... this burden. 

So, if all that went away? If I didn't feel like I was just this worthless piece of garbage dragging everybody down? Maybe. Maybe I'd want to go down to the lake. Maybe I'd look at that Mustang kit and actually want to put the decals on. But honestly, doc, right now, I can't even imagine not feeling this way. I can't imagine a morning where I don't wake up and immediately start beating myself up for being such a failure. It's just so loud in my head, all the time, telling me how bad I messed up. So... Five months, doc. It’s been right about five months now that this whole... this depressed spell has just been hanging over me. You'd think the dust on the model box would bother me enough to at least put it away. But no. Day after day, week after week... it just stretches on. So for five whole months, that Mustang has just been sitting there, and I haven't been down to the water once. Just five months of this heavy cloud hanging over me.

Like some other guy bought that paint. Like some stranger set up that table in my room and I'm just looking at his stuff. It doesn't feel like mine anymore. Like I was saying a few minutes ago, doc... yeah. That's exactly it. It's all the time. I just keep thinking I am no good, you know? I mean, I lost that job, and now... now my relatives, my folks, they have to help me with every little thing. I'm thirty-five years old. I didn't even make it past the eighth grade, I dropped out way back in the day, but I always managed to work. I always pulled my own weight, at least. And now I can't even do that. So yeah, I don't think I've ever felt this low before. This five-month stretch... waking up with that heavy chest every single day, just knowing there's absolutely nothing out there for me... it's definitely the worst it's ever been. There's a difference, you know? Like, I wish I could just push a button and erase myself so nobody had to remember me, but actually taking a step to do it myself? No. I haven't tried to hurt myself, not once in these five months. I just sit in the chair. I just sit there and let the days pass, even though it feels like torture. But I haven't crossed that line, doc. I really haven't.

Well, doc, it's... it's really everything. It's not just that I don't care about the stuff I used to like, it's that nothing feels good anymore. Nothing at all. I mean, you asked about the things I used to enjoy, right? I used to like walking by the lake. There's this little spot, maybe a mile from my folks' place, where the trees kind of bend over the water, and I'd go down there in the evenings. It was quiet, you know? Just me and the ducks, watching the sun go down. It used to make me feel kind of settled. And I had these little model kits I'd work on. Cars, mostly. Classic muscle cars. But now... man, now they just sit there. The models, the paints, everything. I look at them, and it's like... it's like they belong to somebody else. Some other guy who used to live in my room and actually cared about putting a tiny plastic steering wheel into a tiny plastic dashboard. I look at them and I don't feel a single thing. No urge to pick them up, no interest in finishing the ones I started. They're just gathering dust.

My mom made my favorite meatloaf last week—she spent all afternoon on it, trying to cheer me up, bless her heart—and I put it in my mouth and it just tasted like ash. Like cardboard. I chewed it and swallowed it because I didn't want to hurt her feelings, but there was no joy in it. No flavor, really. And watching TV? So, yeah, it's everything. It's like somebody came in and just unplugged me from... from life, I guess. Nothing brings me any kind of pleasure, not the old stuff, not new stuff, nothing. It's all just flat. Just completely, utterly flat and gray, all day, every day.
